messages:
incbot: :rotating_light: Alert — Datadog ingestion delay detected for metrics/logs. Alerts may be delayed ~5–15m. Auto-pager: oncall-sre notified (pagerduty PD-9981). Root ts: 2109876543

alex: seeing it on our dashboards too. metrics for inference-latency are flatlined since ~09:12 UTC. traces still show but no new spans coming in to dd.

jin: confirmed. dd logs show `ingest downstream backlog` errors in the last 10m. Trying to pull recent events in UI keeps timing out.

carla: marking customer-impact potential. We have high-traffic customers (Acme Corp) on dedicated routes — their SLOs might be affected if we can't see errors.

oncall-sre: I'm on it. Immediate mitigation plan: 1) switch critical alerts to CloudWatch fallback 2) enable local metrics shipping to S3 as temporary buffer 3) notify support + customers.

support: pinging Acme SOC now with heads-up. Will include reproduction steps if they report errors.

alex: can we temporarily mute non-critical DD alerts to reduce noise? also add a note to the incident channel so downstream teams don't escalate for duplicate symptoms.

oncall-sre: muting non-prod dd alerts now. Leaving pager for critical errors only.

carla: steps I ran: checked host telemetry -> `journalctl` shows spikes but nothing that indicates app-level drop. app is still serving requests. It's primarily observability ingest problem.

jin: running a quick playbook to re-route alerting:
```
# switch CloudWatch alarms to active
aws cloudwatch put-metric-alarm --alarm-name "inference-5xx" --metric-name HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count --namespace AWS/ApplicationELB --statistic Sum --period 60 --threshold 1 --comparison-operator GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold --evaluation-periods 1 --alarm-actions arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:123456789012:ops-alerts
```

oncall-sre: done — cw alarms now mirror dd critical ones. Confirmed test alarm fired to ops-alerts.

datadog-bot: Support ticket created automatically: DD-INC-45321 — Ingestion backlog in us-east-1. Estimated resolution unknown. Status: Investigating.

alex: good. Next: enable verbose local logging for the proxy layer and start uploading to S3 as Jin suggested. We'll also enable short-term request sampling for traces to preserve at least error traces.

jin: started s3 buffering job: `./shipper --buffer /var/log/shipper --dest s3://redwood-telemetry/tmp/210987` logs show files queued.

carla: small customer impact note: we saw a brief spike of 502s to the hosted API at 09:15 UTC — looks like retry storms from clients when metrics lagged caused throttling upstream. I lowered client-side retry multiplier via feature flag for affected routes.

oncall-sre: opened PD incident with Datadog team, posted link to ticket. Also filed an internal postmortem placeholder: https://redwood.internal/ops/incidents/2109876543 (will update).

support: Acme notified at 09:28 UTC — they acknowledged and are monitoring. They asked for ETA, we said "investigating with provider".

alex: any ETA from Datadog?

datadog-bot: DD status page: https://status.datadoghq.com/ — Ingest backlog incident in progress in us-east-1. Latest update: engineers are working on catch-up and backlog processing. No ETA.

jin: monitoring backlog counters with `dd-agent` is flaky. I'll run one-off pulls of recent traces from the application nodes and upload them to internal tracing UI so SRE can chase errors even if DD UI is lagging.

oncall-sre: handing off to night oncall at 10:10 UTC — leaving a runbook with current mitigations: CloudWatch alarms active, s3 buffering enabled, non-prod dd alerts muted, customer notify sent. Handoff notes -> https://redwood.internal/ops/incidents/2109876543/handoff

carla: quick RCA note: third-party ingest backlog -> observability blindspot. Impact type: monitoring/detection degradation; potential customer-visible metrics gaps and delayed alerting. No evidence of data loss yet (we're buffering), but visibility reduced.

alex: thanks team. if Datadog catches up, we'll validate buffered data ingestion and reconcile gaps. If not resolved by tomorrow morning, escalate to engineering leadership and consider routing permanent critical alarms to multi-provider path. :white_check_mark:
